headline: Rice's new Arsenal deal: reported, not signed
paragraphs: Arsenal provide the day's most concrete transfer story: Sky Sports News reports that Declan Rice has verbally agreed terms on a new long-term contract at Arsenal. The item lists 'Sky Sports' as a second source, but that is the same newsroom as Sky Sports News, not independent confirmation — nothing from a different outlet corroborates the deal. Until Arsenal confirm it, the Rice contract should be read as reported, not done.

Manchester City and Real Madrid both surface in single-source reports with no corroboration. FourFourTwo says City players' agents are positioning clients for free transfers in case of further sanctions — unconfirmed and attributed to one outlet. Real Madrid's Endrick keeps drawing interest from elsewhere: BBC's gossip column linked him with Arsenal earlier in the week, then separately reported AC Milan want him on loan days later. Both are speculative, from the same gossip column, and not evidence of one deal advancing.

Liverpool's only mention in today's feed is a FourFourTwo report that the club will not enter the January or next-summer market to replace Virgil van Dijk — again a single-outlet claim, not a confirmed plan. Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich have no fresh reporting in today's feed; most of the day's volume instead covered the November internationals, Thomas Frank's move to Crystal Palace, and the Fifa presidential contest, none of which touch the six clubs tracked here.
